method_components.name: Orthology-aware cross-species expression comparison
method_components.rationale: All selected hypotheses require reproducible comparisons across four species while preserving species-specific provenance and avoiding unsupported directionality.

method_components.name: Predefined pathway and gene-set testing
method_components.rationale: The hypotheses are defined at coordinated functional-axis level, so pathway-level tests are needed in addition to isolated-gene contrasts.

method_components.name: TNNT3 exon and isoform usage measurement
method_components.rationale: The TNNT3 hypothesis specifically concerns alternative transcript usage and possible exon 3 deletion, which gene-level counts cannot establish.

method_components.name: Cross-species replication and confounding assessment
method_components.rationale: Reproducibility across high-heart-rate species and control of species, batch, sex, tissue, and other metadata effects are explicit falsification requirements.

method_candidates.name: Orthology-aware gene-level differential expression model
method_candidates.purpose: Estimate direction-neutral, cross-species gene-level differences while accounting for species and available sample-level covariates.
implementation_steps: Validate raw-count matrix, sample metadata, gene identifiers, and species labels.
Map genes to stable one-to-one or explicitly qualified ortholog groups.
Construct a prespecified model with species, phenotype grouping, and available technical or biological covariates.
Estimate contrasts and retain effect sizes, uncertainty intervals, and model diagnostics.
Summarize reproducible signals at gene and ortholog-group levels.
assumptions: Samples represent comparable cardiac tissue and biological states.
Orthology mappings are accurate for retained genes.
The contrast and covariate structure are specified before inspecting results.
strengths: Uses the authorized gene-level data binding.
limitations: Cannot establish causality or physiological adaptation.
Results depend on orthology quality and metadata completeness.
Gene-level data cannot test transcript isoform usage.

method_candidates.name: Competitive and self-contained pathway enrichment
method_candidates.purpose: Test whether coordinated signals span predefined cardiac functional components rather than isolated genes.
implementation_steps: Define non-overlapping or explicitly overlapping gene sets before analysis.
Transform gene-level statistics into orthology-aware pathway inputs.
Run competitive and self-contained enrichment tests for each functional component.
Control multiplicity within the prespecified pathway families.
Assess whether signals replicate across high-heart-rate species and components.
assumptions: Pathway definitions are biologically relevant to cardiac tissue.
Gene-set membership is comparable across species after orthology mapping.
Multiple-testing and gene-set overlap are handled transparently.
expected_outputs: Pathway enrichment effect estimates and uncertainty
limitations: Enrichment is associative and not mechanistic proof.

method_candidates.name: TNNT3 exon and exon-junction usage analysis
method_candidates.purpose: Directly test TNNT3 transcript usage and possible exon 3 deletion using transcript- or junction-resolved evidence.
implementation_steps: Obtain transcript- or exon-level abundance and junction evidence for all species.
Harmonize TNNT3 transcript models and identify exon 3 and relevant junctions.
Estimate exon inclusion or transcript usage within species and across the phenotype contrast.
Require independent junction or transcript support for an exon 3 deletion claim.
Assess replication across high-heart-rate species and report annotation limitations.
assumptions: Transcript or junction data have sufficient coverage for TNNT3.
TNNT3 annotations are comparable across species.
Exon 3 boundaries can be mapped without unsupported inference.
strengths: Directly tests the stated molecular mechanism.
Distinguishes gene abundance from isoform usage.
Can provide explicit evidence for or against exon 3 deletion.
limitations: The authorized binding lists gene-level matrices, not transcript or junction data.
Cross-species annotation differences may limit comparability.
Short-read evidence may not resolve full-length isoforms.
alternatives: Species-specific transcript assembly followed by orthology review
required_inputs: transcript- or exon-level abundance data for all four species
missing_inputs: Transcript- or exon-level abundance data are not included in the authorized current-round data binding.

method_candidates.name: Leave-one-species-out replication and confounding audit
method_candidates.purpose: Determine whether pathway-level associations are reproducible across high-heart-rate species and robust to plausible species or batch confounding.
applicable_to: metadata with species, group, sex, batch, and tissue variables
implementation_steps: Predefine the replication unit and minimum support required across high-heart-rate species.
Fit the primary analysis and repeat it leaving out each species in turn.
Audit metadata balance, batch structure, tissue comparability, and potential confounding.
Compare effect direction, uncertainty, and pathway membership across sensitivity analyses.
Classify hypotheses as supported, falsified, or unresolved only using prespecified criteria.
assumptions: Relevant confounders are measured in the authorized metadata.
There are enough biological replicates for species-stratified checks.
Replication thresholds are defined before reviewing results.
strengths: Directly addresses the hypotheses' reproducibility criteria.
Separates robustness from a single pooled result.
limitations: Small species-specific sample sizes may reduce power.

method_candidates.name: Multivariate latent pathway activity model
method_candidates.purpose: Estimate coordinated activity across related pathways while reducing dependence on individual-gene significance thresholds.
implementation_steps: Construct orthology-harmonized pathway-by-sample scores from the authorized expression matrix.
Fit a multivariate model with species and phenotype terms and prespecified covariates.
Evaluate covariance and coordinated pathway shifts across functional components.
Validate latent scores using held-out species or leave-one-species-out sensitivity analyses.
Compare conclusions with the simpler gene-level and enrichment methods.
assumptions: Pathway memberships are sufficiently stable across species.
Latent factors are identifiable with the available sample size.
Model complexity is justified by the number of samples and pathways.
strengths: Can reduce instability from individual-gene testing.
Provides a complementary method for convergence assessment.
limitations: Latent factors may be difficult to interpret biologically.
